Zero thinking is involved in the process, there is no 'emergent thinking' in it, none. The main problem with the premise of this video is that "the only job that has disappeared is elevator operator". That's not the concern that the jobs will entirely disappear. But if one person can now do the job of 10 people, why would any profit based business pay those other 9 people? They certainly wont pay them MORE. The amount of labor required absolutely has a cap, its not infinite. When that threshold is met, there simply aren't enough jobs for everyone anymore. "More jobs will be created". Yes more low paying menial jobs that the unemployed will have to fight for to survive with zero negotiation value. Weve literally been hearing people complain they cant survive on dual incomes for decades, whereas in the 1950s you could buy a house and raise a family working at a gas station. This video is very short sighted about the actual dangers of "AI taking jobs". You also posit that "more equals better" when that couldn't be further from the truth. And this doesnt even get into what happens after we've had multiple generations of people refusing to think for themselves because the AI (controlled by billion dollar corporations) does all the thinking for them.

Great video but imho too optimistic and grounded in questionable premises. Once the AI is capable of doing anything humans do better than all humans, what possible need could there be for humans? It’s not rational to assume augmentation. Replacement is the only rational forecast. You’re using the pre-AI past as your precedent but it’s not a helpful precedent. General intelligence is hyper-revolutionary. It’s not merely industrialisation or automation. The instinct to compare them is likely wrong. So while you’re finding augmentation is the norm now, you’re describing what is very likely a short interstitial period in history. I’d be delighted to be wrong, but I suspect your thesis (and this video) won’t age well. Would love to know your thoughts.
